newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips extend gains, 2nd board off sharply.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips extend gains, 2nd board off sharply.

text.p: Kuala Lumpur blue chips extended their reach into new high ground for 1996, gaining 0.6 percent as foreign and local money continued to pour into larger-capitalisation names.
The Second Board, by contrast, sank another 3.23 percent or 19.73 points to 591.01 in what some analysts termed as an overdue correction for the frothy sector.

The Composite Index picked up momentum from Friday, tacking on 7.66 points to 1,225.62. "Slow, steady climbing" and interest in banking shares helped the blue chip barometer advance, said an institutional dealer with a local firm.
"What we're seeing is a switch from the retailers moving away from the Second Board which has really been volatile," said Jonathan Duckett, a Mohaiyani institutional dealer.

Expectations that stockbroker Rashid Hussain will announce a deal to acquire 75 percent of Kwong Yik Bank and news that Malaysian government economic adviser Daim Zainuddin is in talks to take over Hock Hua Bank (Sabah) Bhd has sparked interest in the financial services group, dealers said.
Hock Hua Bank rose 1.10 to 10.30 ringgit, its foreign shares gained 1.05 to 10.20, Commerce Asset gained 80 cents to 18.60 and Arab-Malaysian Corp rose 70 cents to 12.60.
